work_function: W = 1.786 * 1.5 * sqrt(r-1) + < 2^59.5 (all one-offs worst case) (score = log2(W))
heuristics: H1 (random-function model): with published pseudorandom constants c_j = sha512(...) mod r, walker states collide at the parallel-rho birthday rate t^2/(2(r-1)) under Rayleigh collision times, distinguished-point counts are Binomial(t, 2^-80), and cycle entries occur at the self-pair birthday scale t^2/(2Kr) = 1.717e-05 with waste beyond a 2^-23 budget fraction of probability <= 7.32e-04 (Markov on the bounded expectation). No rescaling of the scalar confines the step set: Part A measures every M <= 2^12 (narrowest window 0.6329 of r; the same check detects the rejected v6 constants at 5.93e-67) and the counting heuristic 32*W^31/r^30 puts expected confiners of width <= 2^240 below 2^-234.

Efficiency (collision-time factor): within the fixed budget the success probability is (1 - 0.012451) * 1 - exp(-(1.5/c)^2/2), so the 0.39 claim holds for every factor c <= 1.4781, computed after all deductions. The only measurement is the toy, which runs the same arena machinery with the same constants construction and measures c = 1.093; the tolerance covers a 35% slower production walk. No external factor enters the model.
limitations: Analytic construction; no production-size execution is claimed or possible.
Single-shot randomized attack at the 0.39 threshold (modeled success 0.5975488280 at the toy's measured collision-time factor 1.093; the claim tolerates every factor up to 1.4781).

The arena is a hard 2^56-record allocation (2^63 bytes, the peak; heapsort is in place with no workspace, and the whole construction sits strictly inside the 64-bit address space); the next append aborts with probability <= 0.011718750 by Markov on the exact mean record count, subtracted.

Standard cryptanalysis (parallel Pollard rho with distinguished points, pseudorandom published constants, an append-only arena and one final sort); the worst-case ledger, the confinement certificate and the post-deduction collision-factor tolerance are the contribution under this cost model.
